hook.text: The Baja 1000 sends trucks, buggies, and motorcycles across a thousand miles of Mexican desert.

buildup.text: There's no closed course—vehicles race through cacti, sand washes, and villages at top speed.

discovery.text: Locals have been known to dig hidden trenches in the route to watch spectacular crashes.

twist.text: The race runs nonstop, so drivers swap behind the wheel to keep going through the night.

climax.text: Finishing the Baja 1000 is considered a greater achievement than winning most other races.

punchline.text: In Baja, just surviving the finish line is the real victory.

quiz.question: What makes the Baja 1000 unique among races?
options: It crosses open desert with no closed course

details.summary: The Baja 1000 is a grueling off-road race through Mexico's Baja California peninsula, covering over 1,000 miles of desert, mountains, and silt beds that destroy vehicles and test driver endurance.
details.whyItMatters: The Baja 1000 is the ultimate test of off-road vehicle durability. No race exposes weaknesses in suspension, engines, and structures as brutally as a thousand miles of Mexican desert at racing speed.
takeaways: The course stretches over 1,000 miles through Baja California
Trophy trucks, motorcycles, and buggies all compete simultaneously
Only about half the starters typically finish the race

faq.question: How long does it take to finish the Baja 1000?
faq.answer: Trophy trucks complete the roughly 1,000-mile course in about 16 to 20 hours. Slower classes can take over 30 hours. Drivers often race through the night in pitch-dark desert conditions.

faq.question: Is the Baja 1000 dangerous?
faq.answer: Very. Spectators, animals, and unmarked obstacles in the desert create real hazards. Several deaths have occurred over the race's history. The remote terrain means rescue assistance can be hours away.
